problem: The statement that the typical default pipe buffer size is 4 KB is outdated; on modern Linux kernels the default pipe capacity is 64 KB.
fix: Replace with: "Pipe buffer size is kernel defined; typical default on modern Linux is 64 KB (can be queried via /proc/sys/fs/pipe‑max‑size)."

problem: The suggested mitigation of using flock() on a FIFO is incorrect because flock does not work reliably on named pipes; atomic writes up to PIPE_BUF should be used instead.
fix: Replace the mitigation with: "Ensure each writer writes messages no larger than PIPE_BUF (usually 4 KB) so writes are atomic, or use a separate synchronization mechanism such as a POSIX semaphore or a dedicated logger process that serialises writes."

problem: The description mentions only System V keys for identifying a segment, omitting POSIX shared memory which uses a name.
fix: Add a sentence: "POSIX shared memory uses shm_open with a pathname‑like name instead of a numeric key."

problem: Units for throughput are not specified; readers may be unclear whether the result is bytes per millisecond or another unit.
fix: Specify: "Effective throughput (bytes per millisecond) = Data size (bytes) ÷ (Write time + Read time + Sync overhead) (milliseconds)."
